help.title: Help — {context}
help.guide.s1.heading: The idea: review at the right moment
help.guide.s1.1: Cadence is a **spaced repetition** app. It helps you remember, for the long run, anything you want to learn: vocabulary, course material, pieces of music, a dance repertoire…
help.guide.s1.2: The idea: you remember something far better when you review it **just before you would forget it**. For each item, Cadence estimates when your memory starts to fade, and brings it back at that moment.
help.guide.s1.3: The better you know an item, the further apart its reviews: a few days, then a few weeks, then a few months. Your time goes to what needs it.
help.guide.s1.4: There is nothing to schedule: come back regularly, even for a few minutes, and review what Cadence offers.
help.guide.s2.heading: The vocabulary at a glance
help.guide.s2.1: **Card**: one thing to remember (a word, a question, a tune…). It has a name and can hold notes, files and links.
help.guide.s2.2: **Deck**: a group of cards reviewed together. The same card can be in several decks without being duplicated.
help.guide.s2.3: **Folder**: holds decks (and other folders). Purely for tidiness.
help.guide.s2.4: **Library**: the list of all your cards, whatever their deck.
help.guide.s2.5: **Session**: a review moment in which Cadence shows you cards one at a time; for each one, you say whether you remembered it.
help.guide.s3.heading: Finding your way around
help.guide.s3.1: Navigation bar (at the top on a computer, at the bottom on a phone): the **house** leads Home, the **list** to the Library, the **four squares** to the Modules. The ‹ › arrows go back and forward.
help.guide.s3.2: The **panel** icon, top left, shows or hides the **sidebar**: the tree of your folders and decks. Its two bottom buttons create a folder or a deck.
help.guide.s3.3: Top right: the **magnifying glass** to find a card, deck or folder (shortcut `Ctrl+K`), the **?** for help on the current page, the **gear** for settings.
help.guide.s3.4: In the middle, the active **profile** (“Default” to begin with). It only matters if several people share the same cards on this device: each then has their own review history (profile menu → “Manage profiles”, where a profile can also be renamed).
help.guide.s4.heading: Creating your first cards
help.guide.s4.1: Open the **Library** and tap **“+ New card”**, then **Create**. Type a name and confirm; you can add several cards in a row without closing the window.
help.guide.s4.2: Each time, Cadence asks which **deck(s)** the card goes into. You can tick none and decide later, or create a deck on the spot.
help.guide.s4.3: Then open the card to fill it in: **notes** (the answer, an explanation…), **tags**, **attachments** (image, sound, PDF, YouTube video…).
help.guide.s4.4: For a question-and-answer card, write the answer in the notes between double bars: `||the answer||`. It stays hidden during review until you tap it.
help.guide.s4.5: **“+ New card” → Import** adds ready-made cards: a Cadence cards file (.cdc), a 6-character **share key** someone gave you, or a list converted by an **AI** (ChatGPT, Claude…) using the text provided to copy. Musicians will also find TheSession and irishtune.info there.
help.guide.s5.heading: Organising into decks and folders
help.guide.s5.1: Create a deck with **“+ Deck”** on Home or in a folder, or with the bottom button of the sidebar.
help.guide.s5.2: To put a card in a deck: from the deck (the “Link an existing card…” field or the **+** button), from the card (the **link** icon under its name), or several cards at once from the Library (tick them, then the **⋯** menu).
help.guide.s5.3: In the sidebar, drag and drop decks and folders to rearrange them, or drop them onto a folder to put them inside. On a phone, press and hold for a moment before dragging.
help.guide.s5.4: A deck's **star** adds it to the **Favorites** on Home, one tap away.
help.guide.s6.heading: Reviewing
help.guide.s6.1: Tap **“▶ Study”** on a deck or folder, or **“▶ Study all”** on Home. You can also review a selection of cards from the Library.
help.guide.s6.2: A window offers a **strategy**: the order in which cards come up. **Optimal**, which starts with the cards most at risk, suits most cases.
help.guide.s6.3: Only cards **due now** are shown. A card you still know well waits its turn, and a card never reviewed is always shown.
help.guide.s6.4: Each card appears **only once per session**. When none are left, “Study complete!” appears: come back later, other cards will be due.
help.guide.s7.heading: Remember first, then rate yourself honestly
help.guide.s7.1: The card is shown with its notes and attachments. **Try to recall first** — find the translation, play the tune… — then check.
help.guide.s7.2: Then say how it went: **✗ Again** (forgotten), **△ Hard** (recalled with difficulty), **○ Good** (recalled normally), **✓ Easy** (instant).
help.guide.s7.3: Your rating sets the next review. For a first review, with the default settings, the card comes back after about **10 hours** for “Again”, **1 day** for “Hard”, **3 days** for “Good” and **2 weeks** for “Easy”. After that, every success stretches the interval.
help.guide.s7.4: Be honest: a generous rating spaces reviews too far apart, and forgetting sets in. On a keyboard: `1` to `4` to rate, `Tab` to skip a card without rating it, `Esc` to leave.
help.guide.s8.heading: Tracking your progress
help.guide.s8.1: **Home** sums things up: number of cards, reviews this week, **streak** of consecutive days with a review, and an activity chart.
help.guide.s8.2: Decks and cards carry **two dots**: the first is **recall** (the chance you remember it right now), the second is **ease** (how easily it usually comes back to you).
help.guide.s8.3: Green = solid, yellow = middling, red = fragile. A card never reviewed has a red recall and a grey ease: that is normal at first.
help.guide.s8.4: Deck and card pages detail these figures; their **?** explains each one.
help.guide.s9.heading: Protecting your data
help.guide.s9.1: Cadence works **without an account**: your cards and history are stored **in this browser, on this device**, and nowhere else unless you ask.
help.guide.s9.2: Which means: if the browser's data is cleared, or you change or lose the device, **everything is lost** — unless you have a backup.
help.guide.s9.3: The simplest option: **Settings → User → Google Drive → Connect**. Syncing is then automatic, and your data can be recovered on another device from the welcome screen: “Restore my data (Google Drive)”.
help.guide.s9.4: Once connected, the **cloud** icon at the top left shows the status: green = up to date, yellow = changes waiting (tap to send), red = error (tap to retry).
help.guide.s9.5: Without Drive: in **Settings → Storage**, the icons next to “User” **export** a backup to a file (arrow up) or **import** it back (arrow down). Do it regularly.
help.guide.s9.6: The **yellow triangle** at the top left means the browser has not guaranteed to keep your data: it could delete it to free up space. Tap it to ask for persistent storage. **Installing Cadence as an app** (the “App” button at the top, when it appears) also helps, and puts it on the device's home screen.
help.guide.s10.heading: For musicians
help.guide.s10.1: Cadence works for any kind of learning, but also offers tools for **traditional music, especially Irish**.
help.guide.s10.2: **Tune import** from TheSession.org (a tune, a member's tunebook, bookmarks or sets) and irishtune.info: cards arrive with their sheet music.
help.guide.s10.3: Playable **ABC scores** (tempo, instrument, loop), and a tune's **opening bars** shown right on its card.
help.guide.s10.4: **Tune sets**: a card that strings several tunes together, with a merged score.
help.guide.s10.5: **Modules** (four squares): the **Tune analyser** recognises the tunes played in a recording or an audio or video file; **Trending** shows the tunes whose popularity is rising on TheSession.
help.guide.s11.heading: Need help?
help.guide.s11.1: The **?** at the top right explains the page you are on: open it whenever a screen puzzles you. This “User guide” tab is always there too.
help.guide.s11.2: In Settings, the small **?** next to a setting explains it. On a computer, hovering over a button also shows what it does.
help.guide.s11.3: The **share** button, at the top left, gives you Cadence's link to pass on, and access to the **community**: news, ideas, questions.
help.home.start.heading: Getting started
help.home.start.1: New to Cadence? The **“User guide”** tab, at the top of this window, explains everything step by step.
help.home.start.2: Home is your starting point: it sums up your work and gives access to your folders and decks.
help.home.start.3: A **yellow triangle** at the top left? It means your data isn't yet safe from being cleared by the browser: see “Protecting your data” in the User guide.
help.home.stats.heading: The dashboard
help.home.stats.1: **Cards**: how many cards you have, and the number of decks.
help.home.stats.2: **This week**: your reviews over the last 7 days; below, the total since the start.
help.home.stats.3: **Streak**: the number of consecutive days on which you reviewed. One review a day is enough to keep it going.
help.home.stats.4: **Activity**: one bar per day (**7d**, **1m**) or per week (**1y**). Tap a bar to see its number of reviews; `Shift`+click (or a long press on a phone) on a second bar selects the whole period. The button that appears opens the Library on the cards reviewed during that period.
help.home.stats.5: These figures only count the active **profile** (shown at the top, in the middle).
help.home.study.heading: Reviewing
help.home.study.1: **“▶ Study all”** starts a session on all your cards. Only those that need reviewing will be shown.
help.home.study.2: To review only part of them, open a deck or folder and use its own “▶ Study” button.
help.home.organize.heading: Organising
help.home.organize.1: **Favorites**: decks starred on their page show up here as shortcuts.
help.home.organize.2: **Folders** and **Decks**: the ones at the top level. “+ Folder” and “+ Deck” create them here.
help.home.organize.3: Drag and drop a row to change the order. To put a deck or folder inside a folder, drag it onto that folder in the sidebar, or use “Location” on its page.
help.home.organize.4: Each deck shows its two dots, its last review and its number of cards.
help.home.dots.heading: The coloured dots
help.home.dots.1: **First dot — recall**: the average chance you remember the deck's cards right now. It drops over time and rises when you review.
help.home.dots.2: **Second dot — ease**: how easily these cards usually come back to you, based on your past ratings.
help.home.dots.3: Green = solid, yellow = middling, red = fragile. A grey ease means no card has been reviewed yet. On a computer, hover over a dot to see its value.
help.folder.what.heading: What is a folder?
help.folder.what.1: A folder holds decks, and possibly other folders. It is only for organising: it changes nothing about reviews.
help.folder.what.2: Cards are not directly in the folder: they are in its decks.
help.folder.study.heading: Reviewing the folder
help.folder.study.1: **“▶ Study”** starts a session on the cards of every deck in this folder and its sub-folders. A card that is in several of these decks is shown only once.
help.folder.manage.heading: Managing this folder
help.folder.manage.1: Tap the folder's **name** to rename it.
help.folder.manage.2: **Location** shows the folder it is in; pick another one to move it (“Home” puts it back at the top level).
help.folder.manage.3: “+ Folder” and “+ Deck” create a sub-folder or a deck right here. Drag and drop rows to change their order.
help.folder.manage.4: The **bin** deletes the folder, its sub-folders and its decks. Cards stay in the Library, unless you tick the option that also deletes those no longer in any deck.
help.folder.list.heading: Reading the list
help.folder.list.1: Each deck shows two dots — **recall** then **ease** (green = solid, yellow = middling, red = fragile, grey = never reviewed) —, the date of its last review and its number of cards.
help.library.what.heading: All your cards
help.library.what.1: The Library lists **all your cards**, whether they are in one deck, several, or none. Tap a card to open it.
help.library.what.2: The two dots before the name: **recall** (the chance you remember it right now) then **ease** (how easily it usually comes back). Green = solid, yellow = middling, red = fragile, grey = never reviewed.
help.library.what.3: **“+ New card”** creates or imports cards: Cadence file (.cdc), share key, AI, TheSession, irishtune.info.
help.library.what.4: Deleting a card here erases it **for good**, from all its decks, along with its history. To take it out of a single deck, use the link icon on its page, or the **⋯ → Remove from decks…** menu.
help.library.search.heading: Searching and filtering
help.library.search.1: Search filters by name or alias, ignoring accents; a card found through an alias shows it under its name. It also accepts the exact number of a TheSession or irishtune.info tune.
help.library.search.2: Below it, filter groups you can unfold: **Decks** (and their folders), **Types**, **Tags**, **Reviewed between** (two dates). A group only appears if it can actually split your cards.
help.library.search.3: Each chip has three states. **1st tap**: keep only those cards (filled chip). **2nd tap**: exclude them (red, crossed-out chip). **3rd tap**: back to neutral. A right-click goes through the states backwards.
help.library.search.4: The small symbol next to “Decks” and “Tags” chooses how several chips combine: **AND** (the card must match all of them) or **OR** (at least one).
help.library.search.5: A **folder** chip covers all its decks; “No deck” shows cards filed nowhere. A faded chip would change nothing in the current list.
help.library.search.6: A “Limited to N cards” chip means the list was narrowed from another screen: tap it to see the whole Library again.
help.library.sort.heading: Sorting and visualising
help.library.sort.1: The sort button picks the order: alphabetical, last reviewed, recently added, importance, recall, difficulty. The arrow next to it reverses the direction.
help.library.sort.2: The value used for sorting (date, importance, percentage…) is shown to the right of each card.
help.library.sort.3: The **scatter plot** icon, at the top right, shows the **card map**: one dot per reviewed card, placed by its **stability** (horizontally) and **ease** (vertically), coloured by its **recall**, and bigger when the card is important. Tap a dot to open the card.
help.library.select.heading: Acting on several cards
help.library.select.1: Tick cards to select them. While a selection exists, tapping a row ticks it instead of opening the card. `Shift`+click (or a long press on a phone) selects a whole range; the box at the top selects every card shown.
help.library.select.2: Action bar: **export** (re-importable Cadence file or share key valid 10 minutes, CSV spreadsheet, text), **⋯** (add to decks, remove from decks, importance, type, tags), **▶** (review the selection), **bin** (delete).
help.library.select.3: If the selection contains imported cards, the **⋯** menu also offers to **update** them from TheSession (name, score, importance, a set's tunes) or to **migrate** irishtune.info cards to TheSession.
help.deck.what.heading: What is a deck?
help.deck.what.1: A deck is a set of cards reviewed together. A card can belong to several decks: it is not duplicated, and its review history stays the same.
help.deck.what.2: **“▶ Study”** starts a session on this deck; only the cards that need reviewing are shown.
help.deck.what.3: Tap the **name** to rename it, the **star** to add it to the Favorites on Home. **Location** moves it into another folder.
help.deck.what.4: The **bin** deletes the deck, not its cards — unless you tick the option that also deletes those no longer in any deck.
help.deck.metrics.heading: The deck's figures
help.deck.metrics.1: **Recall**: the average chance you remember one of the deck's cards right now. It drops over time and rises when you review.
help.deck.metrics.2: **Stability**: how long, on average, a memory holds after a review before falling below your recall threshold. It grows with every successful review.
help.deck.metrics.3: **Ease**: how easily these cards usually come back to you, based on your past ratings.
help.deck.metrics.4: **Mastery X/Y**: X cards out of Y are above your recall threshold (90% by default, in Settings → Study) and so don't need reviewing right now.
help.deck.metrics.5: These averages give more weight to important cards, unless “Weight by importance” is turned off.
help.deck.cards.heading: The deck's cards
help.deck.cards.1: Each row: the recall and ease dots, the name (tap to open the card), the date of the last review and the **importance** ×N.
help.deck.cards.2: **“Link an existing card…”**: type a name to add a card already in the Library. The **+** button creates or imports a card straight into this deck.
help.deck.cards.3: The **list** icon next to the “Cards” title opens the Library filtered on this deck: handy to act on several cards, for instance to remove them from the deck.
help.deck.cards.4: Drag and drop rows to set the **order** of the cards; the “Sequential” strategy follows it.
help.deck.importance.heading: Importance
help.deck.importance.1: Importance is a weight: a ×2 card counts twice as much as a ×1 card. It doesn't change when a card is due, but its **priority** in a session (Optimal and Stochastic strategies) and its weight in averages.
help.deck.importance.2: Every card has a **base** importance: ×1 for a card created by hand, and the number of tunebooks (its popularity) for a tune imported from TheSession.
help.deck.importance.3: Tap ×N to give the card an importance **specific to this deck** (shown in colour); clear the field to go back to the base importance. At ×0, the card is left out of sessions that use this deck as their context (the default when studying this deck).
help.card.what.heading: The card
help.card.what.1: A card stands for one thing to remember. Cadence tracks its review history and works out when to show it again.
help.card.what.2: Tap the **name** to rename it. Just below, the **aliases**: the card's other names, which search finds too. Tap them to add, remove or rename one, or to make an alias the card's name. Further down: the **decks** holding the card (tap to go there) and the **link** icon, to tick or untick its decks.
help.card.what.3: The **bin** at the top right deletes the card for good, from all its decks, along with its history.
help.card.metrics.heading: The card's figures
help.card.metrics.1: **Recall**: the chance you remember it right now. It is 100% just after a review, then drops over time. When it falls below your threshold (90% by default), the card is due again.
help.card.metrics.2: **Stability**: how long the memory holds after a review before falling below that threshold. The longer it is, the further apart the reviews.
help.card.metrics.3: **Ease**: how easily this card usually comes back to you. “Easy” ratings raise it, “Again” ratings lower it.
help.card.metrics.4: **Importance**: the card's weight in sessions and averages (×1 by default). Tap the value to change it; the menu in brackets sets it for one deck only.
help.card.metrics.5: A dash “—” means the card has not been reviewed yet.
help.card.content.heading: Type, tags and notes
help.card.content.1: **Type**: “None” for an ordinary card; “Tune” or “Tune set” for music, which unlock dedicated features.
help.card.content.2: **Tags**: free keywords to sort and filter. **+** adds one; tap a tag to select it, then the **pencil** renames it and the **bin** removes it from the card. Drag tags to reorder them.
help.card.content.3: **Notes**: the **pencil** switches to editing, the **eye** back to display. Formatting works: `**bold**`, `*italic*`, `- list`, `# heading`, links…
help.card.content.4: **Hidden text**: surround a passage with double bars, `||like this||`. It shows as an opaque strip, revealed with a tap — ideal to hide the answer during review.
help.card.attach.heading: Attachments
help.card.attach.1: The **+** adds a **file** (image, sound, video, PDF, text, ABC score…), a YouTube, Spotify, Deezer or SoundCloud **link** (played inside Cadence), or a **card** (a reference to another card).
help.card.attach.2: Tap an attachment's name to open it. The **pencil** renames it, the **arrow** downloads it, the **bin** removes it. Drag rows to reorder them.
help.card.attach.3: For an audio file: **Tempo** slows down or speeds up without changing the pitch, **Transpose** and **Pitch** change the pitch. To loop a passage, set the start `[←` and the end `→]` while playing, then turn on repeat.
help.card.attach.4: A reference marked “(card not found)” points to a card that no longer exists here: the **wrench** offers to re-import or re-create it.
help.card.history.heading: Review history
help.card.history.1: Each square is one review, oldest to newest, in the colour of the rating button used (red for Again, green for Easy…). Hover over it to see its date.
help.card.history.2: Tap a square to correct its date or rating, or to delete it. The **+** logs a review done outside Cadence.
help.card.history.3: Any change to the history immediately recalculates recall, stability and ease.
help.card.links.heading: Links with other cards
help.card.links.1: **Referenced by**: the cards that mention this one in their attachments. These sections only appear when they have something to show.
help.card.links.2: **Played in these sets**: the tune sets this tune is part of.
help.card.links.3: **Detected in**: the Tune analyser recordings in which this tune was recognised. Each row lets you listen to the passage, open that moment in its analysis, download the clip or add it to the card.
help.card.imported.heading: Imported card
help.card.imported.1: The **numbered chip** at the top right shows the source (green for TheSession, blue for irishtune.info); tap it to open the original page.
help.card.imported.2: A right-click (or a long press on a phone) on that chip opens a menu: **refresh** the score, name, aliases or importance from TheSession, or the list of tunes for a set.
help.card.imported.3: For an irishtune.info card whose tune also exists on TheSession, this menu offers **“Migrate to TheSession”**: the card takes TheSession's name, aliases, tags, notes and scores, and keeps its decks and history. Its current content is replaced.
help.card.imported.4: The importance of a tune imported from TheSession equals its number of **tunebooks** (its popularity), hence the high values.
help.card.abc.heading: ABC scores
help.card.abc.1: An attachment marked 𝄞 is a score in ABC format. Once open, it has two tabs: **Sheet** (playback with a cursor) and **ABC** (the text, editable, then “Save”).
help.card.abc.2: Playback: play button, progress bar, **tempo** in %, and loop on by default. Tap a note to resume playback from there; the space bar starts or stops.
help.card.abc.3: A file can hold several versions (settings): switch between them with ← →. The **star** picks the version opened by default, the one used for the opening bars and in sets.
help.card.abc.4: The viewer's **gear** sets your preferences: default speed, instrument, writing out repeats in sets, which tab opens first. The link icon opens the score in the online editor ABC Transcription Tools; the expand icon goes full page.
help.card.abc.5: Editing a score that came from TheSession creates a **copy**: the original stays untouched and can still be refreshed.
help.card.abc.6: **Opening bars**: the first two bars of the tune (of each tune in a set) show on the card, with ▸ to hear them and “ABC” to see the text. Settings → Misc. can also show them during reviews, or nowhere.
help.card.set.heading: Tune set
help.card.set.1: A set strings several tunes together. The **Tunes** list gives their order: drag rows to change it; the bin removes a tune from the set without deleting its card.
help.card.set.2: The **+** adds a tune. Only cards of type “Tune” can join a set; a tune played in a set can no longer change type.
help.card.set.3: **×N**: how many times the tune is played. Tap to increase, right-click to decrease. The value given to new additions is set in Settings → Misc.
help.card.set.4: The **gear** next to “Tunes” turns on the **automatic name**: the set is named after its tunes, and follows them if they change. Renaming the set by hand turns this mode off.
help.card.set.5: The set's score attachment (marked with a gear) is rebuilt automatically from the starred version of each tune; it can't be edited directly. If it was removed, the attachments' **+** adds it back.
help.study.how.heading: How a session works
help.study.how.1: Cadence shows cards **one at a time**, starting with those that need it most. The card is shown with its notes and attachments: **try to recall it before reading them**.
help.study.how.2: Then rate honestly how it went; the next card follows straight away.
help.study.how.3: Each card is shown **only once** per session: once rated, it waits for a later session in which it needs reviewing.
help.study.ratings.heading: The four ratings
help.study.ratings.1: **✗ Again** (key `1`): you didn't remember. The card comes back soon, within hours.
help.study.ratings.2: **△ Hard** (`2`): recalled, but with a lot of effort or hesitation.
help.study.ratings.3: **○ Good** (`3`): recalled correctly, with normal effort. This is the most common rating.
help.study.ratings.4: **✓ Easy** (`4`): instant and effortless. The next review is pushed much further away.
help.study.ratings.5: Too generous a rating spaces reviews too far apart and forgetting sets in; too harsh a rating makes you review for nothing. Pick the rating that describes what really happened.
help.study.during.heading: During the session
help.study.during.1: At the top: the **strategy** icon (with your position in the deck in Sequential mode), the **context**, and **Mastery X/Y** (cards above your recall threshold).
help.study.during.2: **“Skip (no rating)”** (`Tab`) shows another card without recording anything. It is absent with the Optimal strategy, which would show the same card again.
help.study.during.3: **“View card ↗”** opens the card's page; the back arrow returns to the session. `Esc` leaves the session.
help.study.during.4: If “Show the opening bars” is set to “Card and review” (Settings → Misc.), the start of each tune also shows here.
help.study.options.heading: Launch options
help.study.options.1: **Strategy** — **Random**: at random among the cards due. **Optimal**: always the most useful, meaning the most forgotten, weighted by importance. **Optimal stochastic**: at random, favouring the most useful. **Sequential**: in the deck's order, looping (only offered for a deck).
help.study.options.2: **Study context**: “Default” uses the cards' base importance. Choosing a deck keeps only the cards that are also in it, with that deck's own importance.
help.study.options.3: **Weight by importance**: important cards come first. Turned off, all weigh the same.
help.study.options.4: **Exclude mastered** (on by default): leaves out cards still above your recall threshold. Turn it off to review everything anyway, for instance before an exam or a gig.
help.study.options.5: Both switches are remembered for the next sessions.
help.study.end.heading: End of session
help.study.end.1: **“Study complete!”**: no card in this selection needs reviewing for now. Come back later: cards will come back over the days.
help.study.end.2: If this message appears right away, all the cards are still well known. To review them anyway, start the session again with “Exclude mastered” turned off.
help.study.end.3: “N excluded by context” flags cards left out because they are not in the deck chosen as the context.
help.modules.what.heading: What is a module?
help.modules.what.1: Modules are specialised tools, alongside cards and reviews. The current modules are aimed at **Irish traditional music** players and rely on the TheSession.org catalogue.
help.modules.what.2: Tap a module to open it; each one has its own help, via the **?** once inside.
help.modules.list.heading: Available modules
help.modules.list.1: **Tune analyser**: record a session or import an audio or video file, and Cadence recognises the tunes played, with their timings. Ideal to find out what was played and add it to your cards.
help.modules.list.2: **Trending**: the tunes whose popularity is rising fastest on TheSession, over the period of your choice.
help.modules.list.3: A **blinking dot** means a recording or analysis is in progress; it also appears at the top of the screen, and tapping it brings you back to it.
help.modules.pin.heading: Pinning a module
help.modules.pin.1: A module's **pin** adds a shortcut to it in the navigation bar, next to Home and the Library. Only one module can be pinned; tap the pin again to remove the shortcut.
help.modules.pin.2: The pin only applies to this device: the analyser pinned on your phone and nothing on your computer, for example.
help.sessions.what.heading: What the analyser does
help.sessions.what.1: The analyser listens to music and recognises the **Irish traditional tunes** being played, by comparing them with the TheSession.org catalogue. Each recording becomes an **analysis**: the list of recognised tunes, with their timings.
help.sessions.what.2: Only tunes listed on TheSession can be recognised. Recognition runs **on your device**: the audio is sent nowhere. The very first time, a recognition index is downloaded.
help.sessions.what.3: A finished analysis lets you listen to each tune, create its card, attach the audio clip to it, or log that passage as a review.
help.sessions.start.heading: Starting an analysis
help.sessions.start.1: **Start a recording**: records with the device's microphone. On a computer, with Chrome or Edge, the small arrow on the button lets you pick **Device**: the sound played by the computer (a tab, a video…).
help.sessions.start.2: **Import an audio or video file** (MP3, M4A, WAV, OGG, MP4, MOV…): the analysis runs much faster than real time. You can also drag and drop the file onto this page. From a video, only the sound is kept: the picture is often a hundred times heavier, and it would fill up the device's memory as well as your Drive.
help.sessions.start.3: **Import an analysis**: opens an analysis someone shared, from a .cds file or a share key.
help.sessions.start.4: The **tuning fork**, top right, sets the **instruments' pitch**. If the musicians play higher or lower than the written tunes (instruments tuned differently, for instance), set it **before** starting the analysis: recognition depends on it. While it isn't zero, the button shows the chosen shift.
help.sessions.start.5: The **gear**: whether to show the “Detected in” section on tune cards; and, if Google Drive is connected, automatically copy recordings to Drive (with a button to copy those not there yet).
help.sessions.analyses.heading: Analyses tab
help.sessions.analyses.1: Your analyses, arranged like files. The icon before the name shows where it came from: microphone, device sound, or imported file.
help.sessions.analyses.2: “+ Folder” creates a folder; tap it to go in. To go back up, use the path at the top (Home / …) or the “..” row.
help.sessions.analyses.3: From inside a folder, the **pencil** renames it and the **bin** deletes it **along with every analysis it contains**.
help.sessions.analyses.4: Drag and drop an analysis or folder to change the order, put it in a folder, or drop it on “..” to move it up one level.
help.sessions.analyses.5: A new analysis is filed in the open folder. Search, however, looks through every analysis, whatever its folder.
help.sessions.tunes.heading: Tunes tab
help.sessions.tunes.1: Every recognised tune, across all analyses. The number on the right says how many times it was heard; tap the row to see each passage.
help.sessions.tunes.2: Each passage: ▶ to listen, the **score** icon, the **time** (opens that moment in its analysis), the analysis name, then **download the clip** and **add it to the tune's card**.
help.sessions.tunes.3: The round button before the name: **+** creates the tune's card (from TheSession); a link icon means the card exists, and lets you file it in decks. The name opens the card, or the TheSession page if there is no card yet.
help.sessions.tunes.4: Filters: **Analyses** (and their folders), **Types** (reel, jig…), **Keys**, **Other** (hearted tunes ♥, tunes without a card), with the same three-state chips as the Library. Sort: alphabetical, last detection, detection count.
help.sessions.tunes.5: Tick tunes (or long press) then **⋯** to **add them to decks** (missing cards are created) or **add all their audio clips** to their cards. The list icon opens their cards in the Library.
help.detection.heading: Reading a recognised tune
help.detection.1: The **badge** shows confidence: **High** (green), **Medium** (orange) or **To confirm** (grey), with a percentage. An **hourglass** means “consolidating”: the result can still change for a few moments.
help.detection.2: Tap the badge to **check or correct**: the possible tunes are listed, each with its score to listen to. Picking one **confirms** it (the badge becomes a green ✓); picking it again cancels the confirmation. “Another tune…” searches for the right tune if it isn't offered.
help.detection.3: The **name** opens the tune's card if you have one, otherwise its TheSession page. The round **+** button creates the card; a link icon means the card exists and lets you file it in decks. The note icon shows the score.
help.detection.4: The **♥** marks a tune you enjoyed: a personal marker, found again in the Tunes tab (“Hearted” filter).
help.detection.5: Once the result is stable: **−5s / +5s** shift the start (▸) or end (◂) of the passage, the **arrow** downloads the clip, and the **waveform** icon adds it to the tune's card (the card must exist).
help.detection.6: When the analysis has a date and the card exists, **“Log review”** records this passage as a review of the card (✗ △ ○ ✓), at the time it was played.
help.sessionsLive.during.heading: While recording
help.sessionsLive.during.1: Recognised tunes appear as they come. The current tune is outlined, with a blinking dot; “Listening…” means nothing is recognised for now.
help.sessionsLive.during.2: The **pause** button suspends recording and recognition; **Stop** ends and saves the analysis. The gauge shows the sound level being picked up.
help.sessionsLive.during.3: On a phone, **keep the screen on and Cadence in the foreground**: the microphone is cut as soon as the app goes to the background or the screen locks.
help.sessionsLive.during.4: The **tuning fork** can still be adjusted along the way if tunes aren't recognised because the instruments don't play at the written pitch.
help.sessionsLive.during.5: Tap the name to change it; **Folder** chooses where to file the analysis; the **bin** abandons the recording without keeping anything.
help.sessionsLive.during.6: If the tab closes or the device shuts down mid-recording, the recording is recovered the next time you open the analyser.
help.sessionsImport.during.heading: While the file is analysed
help.sessionsImport.during.1: The file is analysed faster than real time; the bar shows progress and time remaining. Recognised tunes appear as they come and can already be played (▶).
help.sessionsImport.during.2: **Cancel** stops the analysis; if several tunes have already been recognised, Cadence offers to keep the partial analysis.
help.sessionsImport.during.3: The **date** is pre-filled from the file: correct it if needed, it is used to date the reviews logged from the analysis. Tap the name to change it; **Folder** chooses where to file it; the **bin** abandons the analysis.
help.sessionsImport.during.4: A file must last at least 20 seconds. Very long files can exceed the memory of some browsers, especially on phones: Cadence warns you before starting.
help.sessionsImport.during.5: The instruments' pitch can't be changed during the analysis: set it beforehand with the tuning fork on the analyser's screen. If it was wrong, “Re-analyze” on the finished analysis runs recognition again.
help.sessionSummary.screen.heading: A finished analysis
help.sessionSummary.screen.1: At the top: the **name** (tap to change it), the **export** icon and the **bin** (deletes the analysis and its audio). Below, the **folder** it is filed in and its **date** (“clear” removes it, “now” sets the current time).
help.sessionSummary.screen.2: The **timeline** represents the whole recording: each band is a recognised tune, coloured by confidence (green = high, orange = medium, grey = to confirm). A tap on a band jumps to the start of the tune, a double tap places playback at the exact spot, and sliding along the timeline scrubs through the recording.
help.sessionSummary.screen.3: The **player** sits just above; the space bar starts or stops playback. The list follows playback: the current tune is outlined, and silences show as “… with nothing detected”.
help.sessionSummary.screen.4: When you arrive from a card's “Detected in” section, the passage in question is outlined in orange.
help.sessionSummary.recording.heading: The recording
help.sessionSummary.recording.1: The icons at the top right act on the recording: **download the audio** (the full file, as is), **re-analyse** and **forget the audio**.
help.sessionSummary.recording.2: **Re-analyse** runs recognition again on the stored audio, for instance after changing the instruments' pitch. The current list is replaced; cards and clips already created are not affected.
help.sessionSummary.recording.3: **Forget the audio** frees the space taken by the recording while keeping the results. Without a copy on Drive, this is permanent: no more listening or clips.
help.sessionSummary.recording.4: With Google Drive connected, the **cloud** copies the recording to Drive (green = copy made), to listen to it on your other devices. Without that copy, the audio **stays on the device that recorded it**: other devices only receive the results.
help.sessionSummary.edit.heading: Correcting results
help.sessionSummary.edit.1: On top of each tune's controls: **“Merge with previous”** joins two consecutive detections of the same tune, and a tune's **bin** removes it from the analysis.
help.sessionSummary.share.heading: Sharing and exporting
help.sessionSummary.share.1: The export icon offers **Cadence Analysis** (.cds, re-importable, with or without the audio, as a file or with a share key valid 10 minutes), **CSV** (spreadsheet, one row per recognised tune) or **TXT** (readable list, to download or copy).
help.trending.what.heading: What this module shows
help.trending.what.1: Trending ranks **TheSession.org** tunes by how fast their popularity grows, measured by the number of **tunebooks** (the site members' personal lists) that contain them.
help.trending.what.2: The data comes from TheSession's public snapshots, published every week. The first opening on a device takes a while, to download the history; after that, only what's new is fetched.
help.trending.what.3: The **refresh** icon, top right, checks right away for a newer snapshot.
help.trending.settings.heading: Adjusting the ranking
help.trending.settings.1: **From / To**: the period studied (the last year by default). Each date is matched to the nearest weekly snapshot.
help.trending.settings.2: **abs / %**: rank by raw gain (the number of tunebooks gained) or by percentage growth.
help.trending.settings.3: **Correct for growth** (on by default): the site keeps gaining members, so almost every tune gains tunebooks. This option removes that general growth — the figure in brackets — to keep only what each tune gains on its own. Without it, the ranking mostly looks like a popularity ranking.
help.trending.settings.4: **Min tunebooks**: leaves out tunes found in fewer tunebooks than this number (300 by default), whose percentage would soar from a handful of additions.
help.trending.list.heading: Using the list
help.trending.list.1: Each row: the rank, the **score** icon (every version of the tune, playable), the **+** button that creates the tune's card (or a link icon if it already exists, to file it in decks), the name, the current number of tunebooks, the gain over the period and a small curve of its evolution.
help.trending.list.2: The name opens your card if it exists, otherwise the tune's TheSession page. The list grows automatically as you scroll.
modules.title: Modules
modules.pinHint: A pinned module gets a shortcut next to Home and Library, so it is one tap away. One at a time.
trending.title: Trending
trending.loadError: Couldn't load trending data — try again later.
trending.deflateHint: TheSession keeps gaining members, so every tune gains tunebooks whether or not it is spreading. This takes that shared growth off, leaving what each tune owes to itself. The figure beside it is the site's growth over the chosen period.
trending.detailLoadError: Couldn't load sheet music for this tune.
sessions.settings.title: Analyser settings
sessions.detectionsOnCards.hint: A tune card then lists the analyses where it was recognised, each detection linking to its moment in the audio.
sessions.moduleDesc: Recognise the tunes played, by recording or from an audio or video file
sessions.recordingIndicator: An analysis is in progress — tap to return to it
sessions.source.device.hint: The sound the device is playing: a tab, a window, or the whole computer.
sessions.source.device.noAudio: No audio was shared. In the browser's picker: select a tab, then tick "Also share tab audio" before confirming. To capture the whole computer's sound: select an entire screen and tick "Share system audio" — Windows only. Firefox and Safari cannot capture tab audio at all; on those browsers, only the microphone and file import are available.
sessions.source.device.unsupported: This browser cannot capture the device's audio. Capture requires Chrome or Edge on a computer; the microphone and file import remain available here.
sessions.recoveryFailed.title: Recovery failed
sessions.recoveryFailed.intro: This recording was interrupted, and rebuilding it failed:
sessions.recoveryFailed.interrupted: The last attempt never finished: the app closed during it, most likely for lack of memory. Retrying may close it again.
sessions.recoveryFailed.audioReady: The audio is still on this device ({size}). Downloading it keeps it, and it can be analysed later by importing it.
sessions.recoveryFailed.noAudio: No audio was found for this recording.
sessions.recoveryFailed.audioUnreadable: The audio could not be read:
sessions.recoveryFailed.confirmKept: The file is safely saved on the device
sessions.recoveryFailed.abandonWarning: Abandoning the recovery permanently deletes this recording from this device, audio included, along with its Drive backup if it has one.
sessions.autoLiveBackup: Back up the running recording to Drive
sessions.autoLiveBackup.hint: Every 10 minutes during a recording, what has just been captured is copied to Drive: if this device loses its data mid-session, the recording can be got back. Around 30 MB per hour, on mobile data and on Drive space alike. The cloud on the recording screen does it by hand, whether this is on or off.
sessions.liveBackup.never: Not backed up to Drive yet
sessions.liveBackup.hint: Send what has been recorded since the last backup to Drive
sessions.liveBackup.failed: The last backup failed ({error}) — click to retry
sessions.liveBackup.needsAuth: Drive needs authorising again — click to back up now
sessions.liveBackup.offer.title: Recording found on Drive
sessions.liveBackup.offer.intro: This recording was interrupted and is no longer on this device, but a backup exists on Drive:
sessions.liveBackup.offer.sameDevice: It was recorded on a device that looks like this one, most likely this one before its data was erased.
sessions.liveBackup.list.hint: These backups delete themselves as soon as the recording is safe. The ones left come from an interrupted recording.
sessions.liveBackup.offer.abandonMessage: This recording's backup will be permanently deleted from Drive. Nothing of it will remain.
sessions.import: Import an audio or video file
sessions.importHint: MP3, M4A, WAV, OGG, MP4, MOV… — from a video, only the audio is kept
sessions.tooShort: File too short — at least {n} s of audio are needed.
sessions.alreadyRunning: An analysis is already running. Finish or cancel it before starting another.
sessions.keepPartial.title: Analysis cancelled
sessions.keepPartial.message: {n} tunes were already recognised. Keep the partial analysis?
sessions.cantDecode: This format cannot be decoded. Supported formats: MP3, M4A, WAV, OGG, MP4, MOV…
sessions.playbackUnsupported: This format cannot be listened to while the analysis runs — the analysis itself works.
sessions.longFile.title: Too long for this browser
sessions.longFile.message: This file is {min} min long. This browser cannot decode it in chunks, so the whole recording has to be held in memory at once — about {need}. Past roughly {limit} min on this device the analysis usually fails. Continue anyway?
sessions.longFile.reason.no-webcodecs: This browser does not provide chunked audio decoding.
sessions.longFile.reason.container: The file format could not be opened.
sessions.longFile.reason.no-audio-stream: No usable audio track was found in the file.
sessions.longFile.reason.codec: This browser cannot decode the file audio codec.
sessions.longFile.reason.no-duration: The file declares no usable duration.
sessions.longFile.reason.unknown: The reason could not be determined.
sessions.wholeFileFailed.title: Analysis failed in this browser
sessions.wholeFileFailed.message: This {min}-min file was recognised, but this browser cannot decode it in chunks, so it had to try holding the whole recording in memory at once (about {need}), and decoding failed. The most likely cause is running out of memory: on this device the limit is around {limit} min.
sessions.wholeFileFailed.hint: To analyse it anyway: split the recording into parts under {limit} min, or import it from another browser or a computer.

sessions.delete.message: Delete "{name}"? The audio and the detections will be lost.

sessions.ranking.viewInLibrary: View these cards in the library
sessions.openDetection: Open this moment in the analysis
sessions.forgetAudio.hint: Delete the audio to save storage — keeps the detections
sessions.forgetAudio.title: Forget audio
sessions.forgetAudio.message: Delete the audio to save storage? The detections stay. You won't be able to add a clip from this analysis to a card afterward, and this can't be undone.
sessions.forgetAudio.messageSynced: Free the space the audio takes on this device? The Drive copy is left alone: it can be downloaded here again at any time.
sessions.audioElsewhere: No audio on this device: it stays where it was recorded, and only the detections are synced.
sessions.syncAudio.hint: Every new recording is copied to Drive: playable on your other devices, and kept if this one loses its data.
sessions.syncAudio.backfill.action: Copy the {count} missing audio files to Drive ({size})
sessions.syncAudio.backfill.partial: {ok} copied, {failed} failed — try again, the others will not be re-sent.
sessions.syncAudio.on: Copied to Drive — click to delete the Drive copy
sessions.syncAudio.remove.title: Delete the Drive copy
sessions.syncAudio.remove.message: Deletes this audio ({size}) from the cadence-data-ext folder on Drive. It will no longer be playable on other devices. The copy on this device is left alone.
sessions.syncAudio.off: On this device only — click to copy it to Drive
sessions.syncAudio.retry: Copy to Drive failed — click to try again
sessions.syncAudio.confirm.title: Copy to Drive
sessions.syncAudio.confirm.message: Uploads this audio ({size}) to the cadence-data-ext folder on Drive, so it can be played on other devices. It stays on this device too, and the copy can be removed at any time.
sessions.syncAudio.failed.title: Drive copy failed
sessions.syncAudio.failed.message: The audio could not be transferred: {error}. Nothing was lost — try again once the connection is back.
sessions.syncAudio.gone.title: Audio not found
sessions.syncAudio.gone.message: This audio is no longer in the cadence-data-ext folder on Drive — it was most likely deleted there. The detections are unaffected.
sessions.reanalyze.hint: Re-run recognition on this analysis's audio
sessions.reanalyze.title: Re-analyze
sessions.reanalyze.message: Re-run tune recognition on this analysis's saved audio? The current list of recognized tunes — including any ❤️ and manual corrections on them — will be replaced with fresh results. Cards already created and clips already attached to cards are not affected.
sessions.share.noAudio: No audio on this analysis — sharing the detections only.
sessions.share.tooBig: The audio would push the shared file over the size limit — unchecked by default, but you can still force it.

sessions.share.wakingServer: Waking up the share server, please wait (up to 1 min)…

sessions.alternates.viterbiHint: Chosen by the recognizer, which also weighs timing/continuity — not just this tune's own mean score
sessions.alternates.notFinalizedYet: Result still consolidating — browsing and listening are available; picking opens once the analysis has settled

sessions.alternates.howToPickManual: Detection added by hand: pick another tune to correct it

sessions.alternates.retracted: This result is no longer valid — the recognizer withdrew it as more of the recording was analyzed
